center.source: 01-RESEARCH.md 'Code Examples' worked example for the Orly-Ville/runway-3 area (48.7233N, 2.3794E), cross-checked against the English Wikipedia 'Orly Airport' infobox coordinate field (48°43'24"N 02°22'46"E → 48.7233, 2.3794 decimal). Used as the query center/radius origin, not the runway itself - the corridor below is the actual runway-3 filter. Checked 2026-08-04.

bbox.source: Computed (not looked up) from the confirmed runway-3 threshold coordinates in 'runway' below: extended roughly 2.5km beyond each threshold along the runway's own bearing (~074/254 TRUE) to include the on-approach and rollout segments, plus a lateral margin. Values unchanged since 2026-08-04 so that adsb-test/RESULTS.md's recorded Phase 1 sampling geometry stays true; this is now a COARSE PRE-FILTER ONLY - 'corridor' below is what actually decides whether an aircraft is on runway 3. Checked 2026-08-04.
bbox.correction_2026_08_27: This block previously claimed the box was 'tight enough to exclude the crossing 02/20 runway' and merely 'not perfectly exclusive' of 06/24. Both claims were measured against real published OurAirports LFPO geometry during the runway3-false-positive debug session and are WRONG. This axis-aligned box is 8078m x 2449m = 19.8 km2 around a 3.3 km runway, and it contains 1935m of runway 02/20's 2403m (80.5%, including runway 02's threshold at 48.717499/2.376700) and 2621m of runway 06/24's 3647m (71.9%). Its corners reach 2229m cross-track from runway 3's centreline. Two real aircraft using OTHER Orly runways were caught being selected as 'runway 3' by a 22-poll live capture on 2026-08-27 (a runway-20 departure at 750m off-centreline and a 02/20-aligned arrival at 611m). Do not treat 'in bbox' as 'on runway 3'.

corridor.source: Runway-aligned corridor around the 07/25 centreline defined by the two thresholds in 'runway' below (bearing 74.41 TRUE, length 3315m as computed from those coordinates). An AIRBORNE aircraft counts as 'on runway 3' when its along-track position is within [-extension_m, length + extension_m] of threshold 07, its perpendicular (cross-track) offset from the centreline is <= half_width_m, and - when the record carries a numeric `track` - that true track is within axis_tolerance_deg of 074.41 or 254.41. An ON-GROUND record (alt_baro carrying the aggregator's 'ground' sentinel string) is instead required to be on the runway's PAVEMENT: within ground_half_width_m of the paved rectangle, i.e. |cross_track| <= ground_half_width_m AND along-track within [-ground_half_width_m, length + ground_half_width_m]. The track gate applies unchanged to both. See ground_gate_derivation below.
corridor.threshold_derivation: Both numbers are read off MEASURED separation between real runway-3 traffic and real wrong-runway traffic, not guessed. half_width_m=500: every real runway-3 aircraft available measures <= 31m cross-track (committed fixtures 39d300 +3.1m, 39dd01 +14.3m, 3985a7 +31.0m; live 2026-08-27 captures 347288 +3.0m and 39cea8 +2..+7m), while every real wrong-runway aircraft observed measures >= 611m (3964e8 -611.3m, 39de4a -750.4m) and runway 06/24's paved surface never comes closer than 887m. 500 therefore sits inside an empty 580m band - 16x above the largest real runway-3 offset and 1.8x below the nearest wrong-runway pavement. axis_tolerance_deg=30: real runway-3 traffic measured 0.0-0.7 deg off axis; real 02/20-aligned traffic measured 56.0-56.7 deg (02/20's axis is 56 deg from runway 3's by construction), so 30 sits inside an empty 55 deg band. IMPORTANT: every measurement behind these two numbers is an AIRBORNE approach or departure track. They were never calibrated for ground traffic, which is why the separate ground gate below exists.
corridor.why_both_gates: Neither gate alone is sufficient, and this is a property of Orly's real layout rather than a belt-and-braces choice. Runway 06/24 is only 12 deg off runway 3's heading (062/242 vs 074/254), so a track gate CANNOT separate it - but its surface stays >= 887m from runway 3's centreline, so the corridor gate can. Runway 02/20 physically CROSSES runway 3's centreline (minimum cross-track 0m, at 1601m along, i.e. mid-runway), so the corridor gate CANNOT separate it - but it is 56 deg off runway 3's heading, so the track gate can. Each gate is blind to exactly the runway the other one catches.
corridor.ground_gate_derivation: ground_half_width_m=75, added 2026-08-27 by the missed-flights-not-displayed debug session, which closes residual (2) below. WHY A SEPARATE NUMBER AT ALL: half_width_m/extension_m describe where an aircraft in the AIR on approach to or departure from runway 3 may legitimately be. Applied to a record already on the ground they are physically meaningless - a +/-500m x 8315m box around a 3315m runway contains taxiways, holding points and apron positions, and effective_altitude_ft() scores every on-ground record at exactly 0.0, so any one of them outranks every real airborne runway-3 movement in select_runway3_aircraft()'s sort. That is the masking mechanism the debug session reproduced against the real code (a departure climbing through 900ft losing to a stationary aircraft at 180m offset). DERIVATION, read off measured separation in the same style as threshold_derivation above: LOWER BOUND - runway 3's own published paved width is 148ft = 45.1m, i.e. a half-width of 22.6m (OurAirports runways.csv, row airport_ident=LFPO le_ident=07 he_ident=25, column width_ft, same download as the thresholds; re-downloaded and re-read 2026-08-27), and the only real on-ground runway-3 record committed to this repo (fixture 3985a7 AFR56XX) measures cross-track +31.1m, i.e. ~8.5m of ADS-B position error beyond the pavement edge. UPPER BOUND - the residual this closes starts at ~150m (see known_residuals). 75 therefore sits inside an empty measured band from 31m to 150m: 2.4x above the largest real on-ground runway-3 offset, 2x below the nearest documented off-runway ground position, and 3.3x the published pavement half-width (so it tolerates ~52m of position error beyond the pavement edge before rejecting). The SAME figure is deliberately reused as the along-track margin beyond each threshold rather than introducing a second tunable: the gate is one concept, 'within 75m of runway 3's paved rectangle'. An on-ground aircraft 2.5km beyond a threshold is on the apron/taxiway network, not on the runway.
corridor.known_residuals: (1) A record carrying no numeric `track` is not disqualified by the alignment gate - it still has to pass the corridor. Measured 21/21 (100%) of live adsb.fi records on 2026-08-27 carried a numeric track, and the pre-existing committed fixtures carry none at all, so this is deliberately permissive rather than a hard reject. (2) CLOSED 2026-08-27 by ground_half_width_m (see ground_gate_derivation). Previously read: 'An aircraft taxiing on a runway-parallel taxiway (~150-200m offset, runway-aligned track) still passes both gates; tightening half_width_m below ~150m would start rejecting genuine approach traffic, so this residual is documented rather than closed.' The premise of that last clause was right and is preserved - half_width_m is UNCHANGED at 500 for airborne records; only on-ground records are held to the pavement, where the 150m floor does not apply because a landing or departing aircraft is on the pavement by definition. (3) CLOSED 2026-08-28 by the same debug session's mechanism-B pass. Previously read: 'NEW, opened by the same change: two aircraft both genuinely on runway 3's pavement in the same poll (e.g. one rolling out toward 25 while another lines up on 07) still both score effective altitude 0.0, so the winner falls through to the seen_pos tie-break. Both are legitimately on runway 3, so either is a defensible thing to display, but the two ADS-B feeds can order them differently and hit poll_current_aircraft()'s disagreement branch.' The FIRST half of that is still true and is not a defect: two aircraft on the pavement do still tie at 0.0, and either is still a defensible thing to display. What was a defect was the arbitration. seen_pos is a property of the FEEDER NETWORK, not of the aircraft ('seconds since this feed last received a position report'), so the two sources ordered one identical reality differently and the cycle was discarded. select_runway3_aircraft() now tie-breaks on hex - a property of the aircraft, identical across every feed and constant between polls - and poll_current_aircraft() now corroborates on the INTERSECTION of the two feeds' candidate sets rather than on their final picks, so a feed that has simply not received an aircraft yet no longer reads as disagreement. See server/plane/detect.py's selection_sort_key() and poll_current_aircraft() docstrings. (4) NEW, opened by that mechanism-B change: STALE RECORDS ARE NO LONGER DEPRIORITISED. With seen_pos removed from the ordering, an aircraft that has already vacated the runway but is still being reported can win an effective-altitude tie against a fresher record. This is an accepted trade, not an oversight: the old behaviour was not reliably better, because being provider-local it oscillated rather than consistently preferring the fresher aircraft. The correct remedy is a staleness FILTER rather than a tie-break, and adsb-test/RESULTS.md's measured position-update gaps (36.2s median / 56.7s max for adsb.fi; 22.4s / 69.8s for airplanes.live) make one unsafe to add on present data - any threshold tight enough to catch a vacated aircraft would also drop genuine traffic. Deliberately not attempted; revisit if a longer capture ever narrows those gaps. (5) NEW, and strictly a restatement of what cross-source corroboration has ALWAYS been unable to do, recorded here because the mechanism-B pass made the corroboration rule explicit enough to be misread as stronger than it is: A SHARED WRONG ANSWER IS UNDETECTABLE. If both feeds carry the same phantom or the same stale position, it is in the intersection and will be displayed with corroborated=True. Comparing two sources can only ever catch them disagreeing; it cannot catch them being wrong in the same way. Checked 2026-08-28.

runway.width_source: OurAirports runways.csv `width_ft` column, same row and same file as `source` below (airport_ident=LFPO, le_ident=07, he_ident=25): width_ft=148 = 45.11m, i.e. a paved half-width of 22.6m from the centreline. Re-downloaded and re-read 2026-08-27 by the missed-flights-not-displayed debug session, which needed a published figure for how far off the centreline an aircraft ON THE GROUND can be while still physically on runway 3 - see corridor.ground_gate_derivation. Recorded here rather than left implicit because it is the physical lower bound the ground gate is calibrated against.
runway.source: OurAirports open aviation data, runways.csv (https://davidmegginson.github.io/ourairports-data/runways.csv), row with airport_ident=LFPO, le_ident=07 / he_ident=25, length_ft=10892 (=3320.0m exactly), le_latitude/le_longitude and he_latitude/he_longitude as recorded above. Cross-checked against the English Wikipedia 'Orly Airport' article infobox (r3_number=07/25, r3_length_m=3,320), which independently corroborates the exact 3320m length for this runway. Note: PROJECT.md's earlier text informally called this runway '08/26' with the same ~3,320m length; the confirmed ICAO heading-pair designator from both sources above is 07/25. Because the length matches exactly across two independent sources and no other Orly runway has this length, 07/25 is treated as the confirmed identity for 'runway 3' rather than the earlier informal '08/26' label - this correction should be carried into any later document update per D-03. Checked 2026-08-04.
runway.correction_2026_08_27: This block previously described the 074/254 heading pair as MAGNETIC. It is not: OurAirports supplies those figures in the le_heading_degT/he_heading_degT columns, i.e. degrees TRUE (074/254 for 07/25, 062/242 for 06/24, 018/198 for 02/20), and the bearing computed directly from the two threshold coordinates above is 74.41 TRUE. The distinction matters because the alignment gate compares against ADS-B's `track` field, which is true track over ground - the same records' `mag_heading` runs ~4 deg lower (249-254 vs a track of 254.2-254.9 for the real runway-25 arrival captured on 2026-08-27), and adsb.fi's `dir` field is not a heading at all but the bearing from the query centre to the aircraft. Verified 2026-08-27.

neighbouring_runways.note: Recorded here because runway 3 cannot be identified without knowing what it must be distinguished FROM. Same OurAirports LFPO rows, same download (2026-08-27). Used by server/test_plane_detection.py as a geometry regression: these coordinates must never be accepted as runway 3.
